knowledge.the_winter_rescue.earthen_smel: Obtaining copper or tin minerals may inspire this idea without prerequisite knowledge. To link, place only a learned raw copper item observation on the tray. Learned clay and sand observations each reduce the wait by one second without tray placement. Starting research requires the idea and all three observations.

A furnace wall must withstand both heat and shrinkage. Compare three clay-and-sand mixtures and inspect their fired samples to find a suitable material.
Learn observations of raw copper, clay balls and sand before starting. Frozen clay can be thawed at a campfire; rotten wood supplies sticks.
Use your 2x2 grid to craft one kiln from each mixture: 3 clay balls + 1 sand, 1 clay ball + 3 sand, and 2 clay balls + 2 sand. After starting research, place each kiln and right-click with 4 sticks to fire for 20 seconds. Collect the samples with an empty hand, check their mixture tooltips and observe all three: two cracked samples and one intact sample. Observations count immediately without keeping, archiving or consuming the samples. Lost samples can be fired again.
Return to the drawing desk to finish the research. You can then craft earthen kiln bricks and form the smelter with an engineer hammer.

Required for linking: a raw copper item observation. Linking aids: learned clay and sand observations each save 1 second; leave them off the tray. All three observations must be learned to start research.
Submit this run's intact trial kiln (consumes one)
You can now craft earthen kiln bricks using the existing bricks and structural metal plate recipe. Trial kilns are not an ingredient.

Arrange earthen kiln bricks in the multiblock pattern and form it with an engineer hammer. Finishing this research normally also learns Earthen Kiln Brick Design automatically, unlocking the brick recipe at the same time.
knowledge.the_winter_rescue.iron_bloomer: An Idea for Iron Smelting

Obtaining iron minerals or common iron products may inspire this idea without prerequisite knowledge. Link learned item observations of raw iron and one of coal, charcoal or coke. A learned copper or bronze ingot observation saves one second without tray placement. Starting research requires the idea, raw iron, ingot and fuel observations.
Bloomery

Complete the airflow game at the drawing desk, then advance manually to the trial. Winning temporarily unlocks the prototype recipe until this run ends. Finishing normally learns the normal tuyere and main bloomery design automatically. No existing furnace is needed.
Learned copper or bronze ingot observation
Learned coal, charcoal or coke observation
Iron minerals or common iron products

Required for linking: raw iron and one coal, charcoal or coke item observation. Linking aid: a learned copper or bronze ingot observation saves 1 second; leave it off the tray. Raw iron, fuel and ingot observations must all be learned to start research.
Bloomery and Tuyere Design

This result is normally learned automatically on completion, unlocking both main bloomery and sandy tuyere recipes. Manually learn it only if it actually remains unlearned in the inbox. Prepare sandy bricks, bronze plates and mortar.
Plan the Airflow
Dig an airflow path through the charcoal bed

Choose Plan the airflow, then hold and drag the left mouse button across the drawing surface to dig. Air flows continuously; dig from the inlet through the furnace-floor charcoal bed to the outlet to record a win automatically. No materials, score or timer are used. Return with the button or Esc, then manually advance to the blowing trial.
Air has crossed the charcoal bed and reached the outlet. The prototype recipe is temporarily available; advance to the next stage.
Dig through the charcoal bed
Test the Tuyere
Inspect the tuyere after this blowing trial

After entering the blowing stage, craft a prototype from 1 sandy brick block, 1 bronze plate and 1 mortar. Place it one block in front of the bellows outlet; replace an earlier placement. Operate the bellows until the prototype becomes a normal tuyere, then observe it on site. A teammate may inspect it too. The observation counts immediately without keeping or archiving it. If lost, craft and blow another prototype without replaying the airflow game. No furnace body is needed.
The tuyere has passed its airflow trial. Finish research to build a bloomery.
Observe this run’s blown tuyere
knowledge.the_winter_rescue.refractory_b: An Idea for Refractory Firing

Raw materials, refractory bricks or direct brick products may inspire this idea. To link, place only a learned sandy brick item or sandy brick block item observation on the tray. Learned kaolin, bauxite and clay observations each save one second. Starting research requires the idea, sandy brick and all three material observations. Existing refractory bricks only improve temperature hints. Raw, crushed, dust, block and frozen-block forms count as the same material family; each family gives at most one discount.
Ordinary Refractory Bricks

Prepare a stone hammer, tree stump, millstone and campfire. Hand-mix 4 kaolin dust, 4 bauxite dust and 1 clay ball for 1 fire clay ball; mechanical mixing still gives 3. Craft the controlled furnace from 6 clay balls, 2 sand and 1 campfire. Advance to firing, then observe this team and run’s successful brick. No submission, consumption or deliberate failure is required.
Learned a kaolin material observation
Learned a bauxite material observation
Learned clay ball observation

Required for linking: a sandy brick item or block-item observation. Linking aids: learned kaolin, bauxite and clay observations each save 1 second; leave them off the tray. Sandy brick and all three materials must be learned to start research. Equivalent raw, crushed, dust and block forms count once per material family.
Controlled Refractory Batch Production

Normally learned automatically, this design enables 16 fire clay balls and 2 charcoal to produce 16 ordinary refractory bricks in the controlled furnace. It only unlocks the new batch process. Existing pottery, blast furnace, industrial kiln and block recipes remain unchanged. It does not unlock high refractory bricks or the IE blast furnace.
Prepare Materials and Furnace
Prepare fire clay balls, charcoal and a controlled furnace

Thaw frozen kaolin and bauxite at a campfire. Crush bauxite at the tree stump with a stone hammer, then mill it; kaolin can be milled directly. Hand-mixing uses all nine crafting-table slots. Advance manually when ready; this stage has no required task.
Advance when ready. Studying existing refractory bricks first will provide a more precise temperature hint.
Fire and Observe
Inspect the intact brick from this firing trial

In trial mode, load 1 fire clay ball and 1 charcoal. Try the middle of 1000–1200°C; start with 1100°C. After 20 seconds, collect and observe the intact sample. A teammate may inspect it too. The observation counts immediately without keeping or archiving it, and the brick is not consumed. If it cracks, prepare another batch and retry. Temperature changes during firing only affect the next batch.

Existing bricks suggest a successful range of 1050–1150°C inclusive; try 1100°C. In trial mode, load 1 fire clay ball and 1 charcoal for 20 seconds, then collect and observe the intact sample. A teammate may inspect it too. The observation counts immediately without archiving it or consuming the brick.
The ordinary refractory brick has passed its trial. Finish research to enable batch production.
Observe the intact brick from this trial
